newsitem.title: USA: Continental pilots say offer falls short.
newsitem.headline: Continental pilots say offer falls short.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. has offered its pilots pay increases of at least 10 percent over six years but that would still keep their wages below industry standards, the pilots' union said Monday.

Continental and the union agreed on Friday to seek federal mediation in their contract negotiations. The pilots' contract with the nation's fifth-largest airline is renewable as of June 30 but talks are expected to run beyond that date.

The company's most recent proposal offers pay raises based on service and type of aircraft flown, the union said. For example, a narrow-body aircraft pilot with 10 years experience would receive a 20 percent raise over six years, the International Association of Continental Pilots said.
The offer also provides for an immediate 5 percent pay raise, boosting the hourly rate to $112.22. That would increase incrementally to $130.36 an hour by July 2002, the union said.

"These pay raises absolutely fail to bring our pilots to industry-standard levels" when compared with current wages of about $153 an hour at American Airlines, $155 an hour at Delta Air Lines Inc. and $158 an hour at US Airways Group Inc., the union said.

"The pilot group would have to wait until the year 2002 before reaching levels of pay that will still fall short of today's industry-standard levels. Of course, by 2002, the industry will have moved even higher," the union said.
The pilots are seeking a pay increase of 38 percent and improved benefits.
While Houston-based Continental is optimistic that a deal can be reached by July, the pilots said the signing date was not as important as the quality of the contract.
Continental declined to comment on the contract proposal or the union's statement.
Continental's class A stock was unchanged at $34.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
